subject: Overload error taxonomy — approval for canary (ADR-014)
body:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Nov 3, 2025 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Overload error taxonomy — approval for canary (ADR-014)

Sean —

We’re at the point where we need a final “yes” on the customer-facing overload error taxonomy so Eng can lock the payload + headers and we can start canary comms.

Key decisions we’re proposing for Hosted API:
- 429 stays reserved for customer-scoped limits (rate limit / quota / concurrency caps that are tenant-configured).
- 503 is used for platform overload / dependency brownouts where we want clients to retry.
- Always include Retry-After on overload responses to avoid retry storms.
- Stable error codes, additive JSON fields only.

Can you review and confirm we’re aligned, especially on the wording and the 429 vs 503 split?

Attachment: overload-error-taxonomy-snippet-v3.md (draft snippet for ADR + docs)

Thanks,
Nikhil
Product — Hosted API
Redwood Inference


---

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Nov 3, 2025 at 10:03 AM PT
Subject: Re: Overload error taxonomy — approval for canary (ADR-014)

Reviewed v3. Directionally good. A few SRE notes to make this safe in practice:

1) Keep 429 strictly “you are being throttled by your plan/policy” (tenant-scoped). Agree.
   - If we use 429 for platform overload even occasionally, clients will treat it as “my fault” and open support tickets / add aggressive retries.

2) For overload, 503 + Retry-After is the right default.
   - Please ensure Retry-After is consistently set across chat/completions/embeddings, including streaming start failures.

3) Wording: avoid internal terms like “circuit breaker open.”
   - Suggest: “The service is temporarily overloaded. Please retry after the indicated delay.”

4) Error codes: keep the top-level short and stable.
   - Prefer something like "overloaded" with a sub-reason rather than proliferating codes.

5) SLO reporting: we’ll classify overload errors separately from “unexpected 5xx.”
   - This needs to match the SLO toolkit rules (so we don’t mask real regressions).

If you incorporate (3) + (4) I’m comfortable signing off today.

— Sean
SRE Lead


---

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Nov 3, 2025 at 11:18 AM PT
Subject: Re: Overload error taxonomy — approval for canary (ADR-014)

Makes sense.

Proposed change to keep it stable:
- error.code = "overloaded" (single code)
- error.type = "overload_error"
- error.details.overload_scope = "region" | "model" | "tenant" (optional)
- error.details.retryable = true

And we keep the message generic + customer-friendly:
"The service is temporarily overloaded and cannot process the request right now. Please retry after the indicated delay."

We’ll also explicitly say: “Honor Retry-After; use exponential backoff with jitter; do not parallel fan-out retries.”

Question: Do you want us to include a “dependency degraded” reason distinct from overload? (still 503 + Retry-After)

-Nikhil


---

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Nov 3, 2025 at 12:02 PM PT
Subject: Re: Overload error taxonomy — approval for canary (ADR-014)

I’d keep the code singular ("overloaded") and allow a sub-reason when we have it.

For dependency issues:
- Still 503 + Retry-After if we want clients to retry.
- Put the distinction in error.details.reason, e.g. "capacity" vs "dependency".
- BUT don’t promise too much precision; sometimes we won’t know quickly.

Also: please ensure we always return a correlation ID in the payload + header (whatever the canonical key is) so Support can triage quickly.

Timeline-wise: if this lands this week, SRE is aiming canary “week of Nov 17/18” in one region.

— Sean


---

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Nov 3, 2025 at 2:26 PM PT
Subject: Re: Overload error taxonomy — approval for canary (ADR-014)

Updated per your notes. Main changes in v4:
- Single code: overloaded
- reason field (best-effort): capacity | dependency | admission
- Explicit: 429 is tenant policy, 503 is platform overload/dependency
- Retry-After required on all overload 503s
- Correlation ID: response header + JSON field ("correlation_id")

Attachment: overload-error-taxonomy-snippet-v4.md

If you can reply “approved” I’ll mark ADR-014 as accepted and let Eng/Docs proceed.

Thanks,
Nikhil


---

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Nov 3, 2025 at 3:47 PM PT
Subject: Re: Overload error taxonomy — approval for canary (ADR-014)

Approved.

Please make sure implementation matches the contract (especially Retry-After everywhere + correlation_id). If we find missing headers in canary, we should treat it as a rollout blocker.

— Sean
